sections.h2: Where is Pueblo, Colorado, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Pueblo sits at the meeting point of the Arkansas River and Fountain Creek, about 112 miles south of the Colorado State Capitol in Denver. It is the county seat and the most populous municipality in Pueblo County.

The city covers about 56 square miles at an elevation of 4,692 feet, on the western edge of the Great Plains where the land starts to rise toward the Front Range. That setting matters when you sell, because buyers in Pueblo are often comparing a house here with ones in Colorado Springs or Canon City, and the drive south on Interstate 25 is short.

Pueblo is also a patchwork. The present city is the result of four towns joining: Pueblo, South Pueblo, Central Pueblo and Bessemer. Bessemer, the steelworker neighborhood on the south side, was the last to join, in 1894. Streets, lot sizes and house styles can change quickly from one part of town to the next, so a buyer pricing your home will look closely at the immediate blocks, not the city average.

sections.h2: How does Pueblo's steel history show up in its houses and neighborhoods?
sections.html:
Steel built much of Pueblo. Colorado Fuel and Iron ran the mill on the south side and, for nearly a century, was the largest employer in the state. By 1909 Pueblo was considered the only steel town west of the Mississippi River.

Workers came from Ireland, Italy, Germany, Slovenia, Greece, Lithuania, Hungary, Japan and many other places, and more than 40 languages were once spoken inside the mill. That mix produced ethnically rooted neighborhoods that are uncommon west of the Mississippi, and many of those blocks still have homes built around the mill's early decades.

The Great Flood of 1921 is the other defining event. Roughly one-third of downtown businesses were lost. The Historic Arkansas River Project, known as HARP, now runs a riverwalk through the Union Avenue Historic Commercial District and tells that story. If you own an older house near a creek or the river, a buyer will ask about drainage and basement moisture, so have what you know ready.

The mill still operates under the name Evraz Rocky Mountain Steel, though with far fewer people than at its peak. The steel-market crash of 1982 started that decline.

sections.h2: Who are the biggest employers in Pueblo?
sections.html:
Healthcare, schools and government lead Pueblo's job list. According to the city's 2023 Annual Financial Report, UCHealth Parkview Medical Center is first, with 4,293 employees.

Public and medical employers tend to keep local demand for housing steady, but a job change, a transfer or a layoff can still force a quick sale, and that is when owners start looking at faster options.

sections.h2: What is Pueblo's weather like, and what does it do to a house?
sections.html:
Pueblo has a semi-arid climate with about 12 inches of precipitation a year and nearly 3,470 hours of sunshine, or 78 percent of what is possible. The sun is the main thing a roof here deals with.

  • Summer highs reach 90 degrees or more on about 71.6 days a year, and 100 degrees or more on about 12 days.
  • The all-time high in the record is 109 degrees, set on July 13, 2003, and the low is minus 31 degrees, set on February 1, 1951.
  • Seasonal snowfall averages 28.3 inches, but it rarely stays on the ground for more than a day or two.
  • Daily temperatures swing by about 32.5 degrees between the high and the low, on average.

Long sun exposure and big daily swings are hard on shingles, exterior paint, window seals and concrete. If you have deferred a roof or paint job, a buyer who pays cash and takes the house as-is will price that in, but you will not be asked to fix it first.

sections.h2: Which schools and colleges serve Pueblo?
sections.html:
Almost all of the city lies inside Pueblo School District 60. Very small portions are in Pueblo County School District 70. Central High School and Centennial High School are the two old city high schools, and their Bell Game, played since 1892, is described as the oldest football rivalry west of the Mississippi River.

Higher education adds a steady rental and starter-home audience. Colorado State University Pueblo enrolls about 4,500 students, and Pueblo Community College has about 5,000 students per semester. Together with the hospital and school district, these institutions give the city a base of residents who rent or buy near campus and the medical center.

sections.h2: How do people get in and out of Pueblo?
sections.html:
Interstate 25 and US 85 run together through the city as one north to south expressway, and US 50 crosses east to west. That puts Pueblo about 115 miles from Denver by road.

  • Pueblo Transit is run by the City of Pueblo.
  • Bustang, run by CDOT, connects Pueblo to Colorado Springs, La Junta, Lamar, Alamosa and Trinidad.
  • Greyhound goes toward Denver, Amarillo and Albuquerque.
  • Pueblo Memorial Airport has daily United Express flights to Denver International.
  • The Union Depot last saw passenger trains in 1971, though Pueblo has been named as a possible southern end of Front Range Passenger Rail.

Freight rail by BNSF and Union Pacific still serves the city, which is worth knowing if a house sits near tracks.

sections.h2: What city rules should a Pueblo house seller know about?
sections.html:
Pueblo's Code Enforcement team handles litter, weeds, parking and storage of inoperable vehicles, and graffiti. If you get a notice and do not comply within 10 days, the recipient can be summoned to municipal court.

That matters if you are selling a vacant or inherited house, because an overgrown yard or a junk vehicle can pile up notices while you decide what to do. Graffiti removal on private property needs a signed release of liability if the city's community service program does the work.

For recording a deed, the Pueblo County Clerk and Recorder says its fee changed to a flat $43 per real estate document on July 1, 2025, after Colorado HB 24-1269. The clerk also notes that any document conveying ownership of real property must pay the state documentary fee under C.R.S. 39-13-102, which is $0.01 per $100, with no fee when the transaction is $500 or less. Your title company handles this at closing, but it helps to know the amounts. Pueblo County's recording phone line is 719-583-6507.

You can read the fee schedule on the Pueblo County Clerk and Recorder's page.

sections.h2: What is a cash sale like for a Pueblo homeowner?
sections.html:
A cash sale means the buyer does not need a mortgage, so there is no loan approval or lender appraisal to wait on. You tell the buyer about the house, the buyer looks at it, and you either accept an offer or you do not.

  • You do not need to repair or clean the house first.
  • You choose a closing date that works with your move.
  • A title company still prepares the deed and records it with the county.
  • You can compare the offer against listing with an agent before you decide.

Sellers in Pueblo most often come to us with an inherited house, tenants who left damage, a vacant property that has drawn code notices, or a mortgage that has fallen behind.

sections.h2: Pueblo's utilities and local energy plans
sections.html:
Black Hills Energy is Pueblo's electric franchisee. In February 2017 the city council voted to commit to 100 percent renewable energy by 2035, and Pueblo County commissioners joined in April 2018. The Comanche Solar Project south of Pueblo was announced as the largest solar farm east of the Rocky Mountains at the time it broke ground in 2015.

For a seller, utilities mean you should schedule a final meter reading and transfer service on your closing date so you are not billed after the keys change hands.

faqs.q: How many people live in Pueblo, Colorado?
faqs.a: The 2020 Census counted 111,876 residents in Pueblo, which made it the ninth largest city in Colorado. The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate, shown at the top of this page, is 110,404.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Pueblo house if it has code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. A buyer who pays cash and buys as-is can take a house with open notices for litter, weeds or inoperable vehicles. Pueblo's code team gives 10 days to comply before a municipal court summons, so deal with any open notice or talk to the buyer about it early.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Pueblo County?
faqs.a: Pueblo County charges a flat $43 per real estate document since July 1, 2025. The state documentary fee under C.R.S. 39-13-102 is $0.01 per $100 on the transaction, with none owed at $500 or less. The title company usually collects both.

faqs.q: Does Pueblo's climate affect what a buyer will offer?
faqs.a: It can. Pueblo averages about 12 inches of precipitation a year and has roughly 72 days at or above 90 degrees, so roofs, paint and windows take heavy sun wear. A cash buyer will price those repairs into the offer instead of asking you to fix them.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Pueblo house in?
faqs.a: Almost all of the city is in Pueblo School District 60, and very small portions are in District 70. Check the district's address lookup if you live near the city edge.
